rationale: Both independently converge on the same core issues (realtime slot/config mismatch, v2-codec-tried-first misclassifying legacy checkpoints, NPU seq_token_counts gap, talker_mtp ignoring temperature/top_k/top_p, WER-fallback silently corrupting eval audio), matching several ground-truth findings (hsliuustc0106's v2-codec High, linyueqian's WER-fallback note) and giving good cross-validation that both are grounded rather than fabricated. Neither catches the cumulative/delta chunk-rewind bug or the ceil/floor audio_tokenizer_v2.py:949 latent bug from the ground truth. Y is more rigorous: it explicitly re-verifies claims against current code state (confirming the abort-release/slot-leak concern was actually fixed, stop-token pinning added, seed rename complete) with literal code-quote evidence per finding, and uniquely catches a real test-coverage gap (talker_mtp_accepts_req_infos not exercised by the updated test). X is well-organized and highly actionable but includes at least one speculative claim (a second slot-leak mechanism) that appears to conflict with Y's verified finding that abort-release is correctly wired, slightly hurting its precision. Neither has a labeled LATENT GAP CHECK section.
